records.title: YouTube Help - Add video thumbnails
records.summary: YouTube's help page for custom video and Shorts thumbnails: who can upload them, recommended resolution, file size limits per device, aspect ratios and the policy on strikes.
records.why_it_matters: It is the target an agent should render a thumbnail to, and it says 16:9 thumbnails on vertical videos get replaced by a 4:5 crop in some feeds.
records.fit_notes: Render 3840x2160 (or 2160x3840 for Shorts) and export JPG or PNG under 2 MB if the upload may come from a phone; desktop allows 50 MB. Many guides still say 1280x720 from memory; this page asks for larger. Keep the subject and text inside a 4:5 centre crop when the video is vertical. Custom thumbnails need a verified account. A thumbnail that breaks Community Guidelines can earn a strike. Limits change; re-check before a launch.

claims.text: YouTube recommends 3840x2160 for video thumbnails and 2160x3840 for Shorts, with a 640 px minimum.
claims.quote: Have a resolution of 3840 x 2160 pixels for videos and 2160 x 3840 for Shorts, with a minimum width of 640 pixels for videos and a minimum height of 640 pixels for Shorts.
claims.locator: Custom thumbnail best practices, Image size & resolution

claims.text: The upload limit is 2 MB from mobile and 50 MB from desktop.
claims.quote:
Mobile: 2 MB for video thumbnails or 10 MB for podcasts.
Desktop: 50MB for video, Shorts, and podcast thumbnails.
claims.locator: Custom thumbnail best practices, Image size & resolution

claims.text: A 16:9 custom thumbnail on a vertical video is replaced by an auto-generated 4:5 one on home, explore and subscription pages.
claims.quote: Note: Vertical videos with 16:9 custom thumbnails will be replaced by an auto-generated 4:5 thumbnail on the home, explore, and subscription pages.
claims.locator: Custom thumbnail best practices, note under aspect ratios

checked.what: YouTube Help article 72431 (custom thumbnails), best-practices and policy sections, against the claims
